story: Gary is at his workbench at home, double-checking solder joints and labeling the wiring harness for a light strip and speaker module with the kind of focus he usually saves for crossword puzzles. Donna has headed over to Magnolia Loop, where Hal is counting the pink plastic flamingo flock one by one from left to right and jotting down the total. Rosa, meanwhile, is resting her feet on a bench in the Town Square, content to sit a while and think through the plans for Saturday's parade.
events: Gary (gary workbench): Double-check solder joints and label the wiring harness for the light strip and speaker module
Donna headed to Magnolia Loop (the street).
Hal (donna flamingo flock): Count each flamingo once, left to right, and write down the total
Rosa (square benches): Sit down for a few minutes to rest my feet and think through Saturday's parade plan

gary.thought_process: I'm home at 7 PM with no one around and still no approval on the application, so the cart stays parked. I already bench-built the light strip wiring and speaker module last tick, and the smart move is to keep working on the bench where nothing is visible from the street. I can verify the connections on the bench so everything's ready the minute Architectural Review signs off. Amplified sound is fine before 10 PM, but I'll keep the test low anyway. Staying busy with something useful beats sitting around lonely.

parameters.content: Double-check solder joints and label the wiring harness for the light strip and speaker module

donna.thought_process: It's 7:17 PM and I've been drilling dinks and third-shot drops for hours with no Gary in sight. I've already reserved the court, studied the ladder board, and warmed up. Nobody's around to talk to, so I shouldn't keep repeating the same drills. Smart move: head back out toward Magnolia Loop, track Gary down, and nudge him about the Halloween cart parade and our practice, instead of standing here talking to myself.

parameters.content: Gary hasn't shown, so I'm going to find him on the Loop and sort out our practice and the parade cart.

hal.thought_process: I've counted those flamingos three ticks running and keep losing track. Time to count once and record it properly, since I can't report a violation without a firm number. Nobody's around, which suits the job. L-02 caps ornaments at three visible from the street, and I intend to have the count on paper before I go to the committee. I'll still speak to Donna before filing, but evidence first.

parameters.content: Count each flamingo once, left to right, and write down the total

rosa.thought_process: I just signed the parade cart up for Saturday's 6 PM parade, and the review folder went in at the desk earlier. The Town Square is empty, so there's nobody to talk to, and I've been on my feet all day. Gary and Donna are my teammates and I want them to see the sign-up is done. The only thing left tonight is to wait for Review's answer. Rather than keep poking at the sign-up table, I'll sit on a bench a minute and take in the quiet before heading home to tell Gary and Donna the news in person.

parameters.content: Sit down for a few minutes to rest my feet and think through Saturday's parade plan

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
